title: Records emit through the logging companion; the fallback stderr path fires only when no companion is applied
asA: operator debugging why an error record did not appear in the log ingestion pipeline
iWant: records to emit exclusively through the applied logging companion's factory (never direct stderr) when a companion is applied
soThat: records land in the same pipeline as every other log line and inherit the companion's redaction, correlation and stamping discipline

acceptanceCriteria.description: When a logging companion is applied on the project, the record emission path calls the companion factory's error() method; process.stderr.write and console.error carry no line from the boundary. When no logging companion is applied, the boundary falls back to a single-line JSON emission on stderr with a documented warning line ('no logging companion applied; emitting error record on stderr').
acceptanceCriteria.given: two fixture applications: one with a logging companion applied, one without
acceptanceCriteria.when: an error is emitted from the boundary
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first case emits via the logging companion (nothing on stderr from the boundary itself); the second case emits one JSON line on stderr with the warning

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a project WITHOUT a logging companion applied, when the boundary constructs a record and reaches the emission path, the fallback stderr path writes exactly ONE line of newline-terminated JSON to stderr per record (a single `JSON.stringify(record)` call), and the applying project's guide names the gap as a known state; no double-emission, no console.error mirror, no additional plain-text prefix.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a project with no logging companion applied and a constructed record
acceptanceCriteria.then: exactly one newline-terminated JSON line is written to stderr and no other writer fires

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a project WITH a logging companion applied, when a caller elsewhere in the codebase calls `console.error(<message>)` directly (not through the boundary), the boundary contract does NOT intercept or double-emit that call; the direct console.error call remains a documented anti-pattern the applying project's linter or code review catches, not something the boundary silently rewrites.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a project with a logging companion applied and a direct console.error call in application code (not through the boundary)
acceptanceCriteria.then: the boundary contract does not intercept or route it through the companion; the direct call remains visible for lint or review to catch (per REQ-004's refusal wording)

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a logging companion whose factory `error()` method itself throws (a rare defect in the applied companion), when the boundary attempts to emit, then the boundary catches the companion's failure, falls back to the one-line stderr JSON path for the record AND writes exactly one additional stderr line naming the companion failure so the operator can spot the double outage; the process does not crash on the companion's throw.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a logging companion applied whose error() method itself throws when called
acceptanceCriteria.when: the boundary attempts to emit through it
acceptanceCriteria.then: the boundary catches the throw, emits the record via the fallback stderr JSON path, and writes one additional stderr line naming the companion failure; the process continues
